CodeOptions.startLineNumber.description: Displayed number assigned to the first source line, defaulting to 1. Line-based annotation methods use this displayed numbering even when line numbers are hidden.

Code.startLineNumber.description: Base displayed line number. Methods translate a displayed line into a source-array offset by subtracting this value; it is not a zero-based source index.

Code.focusOn.description: Keep an inclusive displayed-line range opaque and dim other code tokens and line numbers to alpha 0.3.

parameters.endLine: Displayed end line, inclusive. Reversed endpoints are normalized and the range is clipped to available lines.

Code.focusOn.returnsDescription: No value. A completely out-of-range selection dims every line.
notes: This changes token paint and line-number alpha; it does not hide or delete source text. Use clearFocus to restore full opacity.

Code.clearFocus.description: Set code token and line-number alpha back to 1. This restores full opacity rather than remembering arbitrary alpha values from before focusOn.

Code.scrollToLine.description: Move the code's scroll group vertically so the selected source row occupies the first-row position.

parameters.lineNum: Displayed line number. Values outside the source range are clamped to the first or last row.

Code.scrollToLine.returnsDescription: No value; the transform changes immediately.
notes: This moves the group containing text and annotations; it is distinct from browser scrolling or changing the source string.

Code.getScrollAnimation.description: Create a StateAnimation targeting the scroll group's vertical position for a displayed line.

parameters.lineNum: Displayed line number; clamped to the first/last source row.
parameters.options: Animation duration, easing and other StateAnimation options. Duration uses milliseconds.

Code.getScrollAnimation.returnsDescription: A StateAnimation for Scene.play. Creating it leaves the scroll group's current transform unchanged.

Code.extractText.description: Create a separately addressable Entity containing a matching substring's styled text and add it to this code's scroll group.

parameters.targetText: Nonempty literal substring. Search is case-sensitive and each match stays within one source line.
parameters.occurrence: Positive one-based match number, defaulting to 1.
parameters.removeOriginal: Hide the original matching glyph paths when true; defaults to false. The underlying code string remains unchanged.

Code.extractText.returnsDescription: The child Entity containing extracted Text fragments, or null when the requested match cannot be extracted.
notes: The initial lookup counts matches across the whole source, but this implementation repeats the same occurrence count inside the selected line. A later match on another line can therefore return null or select a different local match. Prefer extractTextByIndices when selecting an exact editor range.
The returned entity is still a child of scrollGroup, so it follows the code's transforms and scrolling. Rebuilding the Code replaces that hierarchy; retain references only for the current build.

Code.extractTextByIndices.description: Create a styled text fragment from an exact displayed line and half-open source-column range.

parameters.lineNum: Displayed line number, respecting startLineNumber. An invalid line returns null.
parameters.startCol: Zero-based UTF-16 offset into the original line, before tab expansion. Clamped into the line.
parameters.endCol: Exclusive UTF-16 end offset. Clamped to at least the start and at most the original line length.
parameters.removeOriginal: Hide the selected original glyph paths when true, without deleting characters from the stored source string.

Code.extractTextByIndices.returnsDescription: An Entity added to the code's scroll group, or null for an invalid line or empty range.
notes: Tabs count as one source code unit and are expanded to tabSize spaces for geometry. Surrogate pairs and combining characters need application-side range handling; these offsets are not grapheme indices.
The extraction copies token text and colors into new Text children. Whitespace-only intersections do not produce a visible Text child, although a nonempty selection can still return an empty group.
